Design review took three rounds: r1 and r2 asked for changes (r1 3 HIGH/6 MED/1 LOW, r2 4 HIGH/6 MED/4 LOW) and both were answered by revising the LLD; r3 ended incomplete with 0 HIGH, 4 MED, 6 LOW and its framing chunk returned placeholder text, so that chunk was not reviewed. summary.prose: Completion stops failing because of an unrelated unreadable head: the roll-up counts unreadable heads only of the kind it is counting. The two old-shape amendment records are repaired by a new, tested repair function that converts them and gives them their lifecycle, so they read as approved with the original approver's name. The repair works on a repository that is already converted, which the full conversion cannot. The roll-up is the sc4 lifecycle contract of the approved epic one-common-model-every-artifact and the conversion code belongs to that epic's s9; this Story keeps the sc4 signature and changes only which unreadable heads block.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Stop flat amendment heads from blocking every completion roll-up

api.name: countedChildren
api.signature: async function countedChildren(id: string, kind: 'TASK' | 'STORY', reader: ChildStatusReader): Promise<Status[]>

parameters.name: kind
parameters.purpose: The child kind that counts towards the unit's completion.

parameters.name: reader
parameters.purpose: Lists the unit's children and unreadable heads, and reads child statuses.

returns.meaning: Statuses of the counted children, excluding withdrawn and superseded.

errors.condition: An unreadable head whose id kind is the counted kind, or a counted child whose status cannot be read.

preconditions: Module-private; reached through the exported rollUp(id, reader, evidence)
reader.childrenOfStrict(id) returns the unit's children and every unreadable head id in the artifacts folder
postconditions: An unreadable head whose id kind differs from the counted kind never makes the call throw
An unreadable head of the counted kind still makes the call throw, as before

api.name: migrateHeads
api.signature: export async function migrateHeads(repo: string, deps: ConversionDeps, seams: MigratedHeadSeams | undefined, only?: ReadonlySet<string>): Promise<number>

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: History, clock and actor for the migrated entries.

parameters.name: seams
parameters.purpose: Test seam between the log append and the head write.

parameters.name: only
parameters.purpose: When given, only heads with these artifact ids are examined.

errors.condition: A head examined has no meta and body objects.
writeMigratedHead refuses because the migration would change the stored revision, status or approval.

preconditions: The full conversion passes no filter and behaves exactly as before
postconditions: Without `only`, every head with no lifecycle or with legacy fields is migrated as before
With `only`, heads outside the set are not read or written

api.name: backfillHead

parameters.name: input
parameters.purpose: The raw head, whether it has a log, the clock and the migration actor.

returns.meaning: The converted head with its lifecycle, the legacy fields it removed and the log entries to append.

errors.condition: The head has no meta and body objects.

postconditions: When the head's body.approvedBy is a non-empty string and the head is approved, lifecycle.approval.by is a person actor named by that string instead of the fixed legacy actor
Every head without a string body.approvedBy gets exactly the lifecycle it got before
The amendment store therefore reads the original approver's name

api.name: repairFlatAmendments
api.signature: export async function repairFlatAmendments(repo: string, deps: ConversionDeps): Promise<{ converted: string[]; problems: ConversionProblem[] }>

parameters.name: repo
parameters.purpose: Absolute repo path; any schema version.

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: History, clock and actor used by the lifecycle migration.

returns.meaning: Ids of the flat amendments written as heads in this call, and the flat amendments that could not be converted.

errors.condition: An amendment head cannot be read for the lifecycle migration.
The lifecycle migration of an amendment head is refused.

preconditions: None on the content of the flat records: one that cannot be converted is returned in problems
postconditions: Every amendment head that lacks a lifecycle or carries legacy fields, converted in this call or earlier, ends with a lifecycle and none of the legacy stamps
An approved amendment's lifecycle keeps its original approval time and the approver's name
A flat amendment that cannot be converted is left untouched and listed in problems
Running it again converts and migrates nothing

api.name: applyAmendments

parameters.name: repo
parameters.purpose: Absolute repo path whose flat amendment heads are converted.

returns.meaning: How many flat amendments were written as heads.

postconditions: Unchanged by this Story; it writes converted heads without a lifecycle and drops conversion problems, which is harmless for the full conversion because applyConversion refuses the whole conversion on any plan problem before calling it

dataModelChanges.details: Each record moves from the flat shape to {meta, body, citations}; meta gains lifecycle (status approved, approval at the original approvedAt by a person actor named by the original approvedBy) and loses the legacy approval stamps; body keeps approvedBy. The id, proposal and rationale are unchanged. Invariant it might break: the amendment store reads approval only from meta.lifecycle and takes the approver from lifecycle.approval.by first. No new entity and no relationship change, so no ER definition is needed.

errorCases.scenario: The lifecycle migration of an amendment head is refused (the head cannot be read, or writeMigratedHead refuses because the migration would change the stored revision, status or approval)

errorCases.response: The migration pass completes them; the ids it migrates are every amendment head in that state
errorCases.userImpact: None beyond running the repair again

migration.stateBefore: Every Story or Task completion in the repo fails because the child scan lists AMD-86197ac660732ceb-1 and -2 as unreadable (flat records with no meta and body) and countedChildren throws on any unreadable head (src/workflow/artifact-core/store.ts:130-161, src/workflow/artifact-core/lifecycle.ts:303-323). The amendment store refuses the two records. The full conversion cannot repair them: it does nothing at schema version 2 (src/workflow/convert/apply.ts:103-115, src/workflow/convert/plan.ts:120-125). The lifecycle migration that a converted head needs is private to apply.ts (src/workflow/convert/apply.ts:84-98), and it stamps the approval with the fixed legacy actor (src/workflow/convert/backfill.ts:39, src/workflow/convert/backfill.ts:73-135), which the amendment store would read as the approver (src/workflow/amendments/store.ts:128-158).
migration.stateAfter: countedChildren throws only for an unreadable head of the counted kind, so unrelated unreadable heads do not block completion. The two amendments are heads with a lifecycle (approved, at their original approval time, with a person actor named by the original approvedBy), readable by the amendment store. A tested repair function exists for any future flat amendment on a converted repo.

migrationSteps.action: Narrow the roll-up so only unreadable heads of the counted kind block it, keeping the sc4 signature; add the tests for it through rollUp; commit.

Make backfillHead name the approval actor from a non-empty string body.approvedBy on an approved head and keep the legacy actor otherwise; export the lifecycle migration with an optional id filter, leaving the full conversion's call unchanged; add the repair function; add its tests on a temporary repository whose schema marker is written at version 2; commit.

Run the repair through a one-off script (confirmed by the user on 2026-11-04) on a copy of this repository first, and compare the two amendment heads before and after: id, proposal, rationale and approval time unchanged; the approver reads as the original name 'Subho Ghosh (in-chat approval)'; lifecycle added; legacy stamps gone. The copy is the preview, because the repair has no preview mode.

Run the repair on this repository with the same script, commit the two rewritten files so git history holds the flat originals, and confirm that approving a BUILD no longer needs the move-aside workaround.
prerequisiteFlags: step 3 comparison shows only the expected differences

migrationSteps.action: Record in the BUILD record that the writer of the flat shape after 2026-10-22 is unverified and name the likely cause (an older daemon build handling the amendments).

migration.backwardCompat: No public API changes. The store contract, the strict scan result and the sc4 signature are unchanged. migrateHeads gains an optional trailing parameter and the full conversion calls it as before. backfillHead's output changes only for an approved head whose body.approvedBy is a non-empty string, which in this repository means amendments, and only in the name on the approval actor; it affects the full conversion only if it is run again on an unconverted repository. The two amendments keep their ids, proposals and approval times, so references to AMD-86197ac660732ceb-1 and -2 still resolve; their file shape changes from flat to head.

alternativesConsidered.name: Narrow the roll-up only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The roll-up ignores unreadable heads whose id kind is not the counted kind; the two amendments are left flat.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Inside the sc4 roll-up (countedChildren, reached through rollUp) keep throwing UnreadableChildError only for unreadable ids of the counted kind (TASK or STORY) and for counted children whose status cannot be read; an unreadable head of another kind no longer blocks. The store scan, the sc4 signature and the two flat amendment records are not touched.
pros: A genuinely unreadable Task or Story head still blocks
cons: The two approved amendments stay unreadable to the amendment store
Leaves old-shape records in the repo
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Stops the failure but leaves the two approved records unreadable.

alternativesConsidered.name: Narrow the roll-up, repair the amendments and keep their approver
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: a1 plus a tested repair function; the lifecycle migration takes the approval actor from body.approvedBy when it is a string.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Do a1. Add an exported repairFlatAmendments(repo, deps) in src/workflow/convert that converts flat amendments with the existing flatToHead, writes them, returns the conversion problems, then runs the existing lifecycle migration over every amendment head that has no lifecycle or still carries legacy fields (not only the ones converted in this call, so a crash between the two writes is finished on the next run). Export migrateHeads with an optional id filter for that. Change backfillHead so that, when body.approvedBy is a non-empty string, the lifecycle's approval actor is a person actor named by it instead of the fixed legacy actor; heads without it keep the legacy actor. The repair is run through a one-off script, first on a copy.
pros: Amendments come back readable and approved with the original approver visible to the amendment store
Problems are reported, and a crash between the two writes is finished by running again
cons: Touches backfillHead, which the full conversion also uses; only heads with a string body.approvedBy (amendments) change
Rewrites two approved records (the originals stay in git history)

alternativesConsidered.name: Narrow the roll-up and repair the amendments, leaving the approver as the legacy actor
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: a2 without the backfillHead change; the reader shows the approver as legacy:unknown.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Do a1 and the repair of a2, but leave backfillHead alone. The original approver stays in body.approvedBy but the amendment store reads lifecycle.approval.by first, so it reports the approver as legacy:unknown for these two amendments.
pros: No change to backfillHead or the full conversion
cons: The approver of two approved amendments reads as legacy:unknown to the store and its consumers
The original name survives only in the body
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Same as a2 without touching backfillHead, at the price of reporting the approver as legacy:unknown.

alternativesConsidered.name: Repair by a one-off script with its own copy of the migration
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: a1 plus an untested script that duplicates the conversion and the lifecycle step.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Do a1. For the data, write a script outside the product source that reimplements the conversion and the lifecycle step for the two ids and run it once.
pros: No new exported code in the product
cons: The next flat head needs the same hand work
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Duplicates logic that already exists and is tested.
